speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me determine the cause, could you describe exactly what these episodes feel like and how long they last? Also, do you notice any triggers such as turning your head quickly or standing up?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Given your age, position-dependent symptoms, and history of hearing loss, could you tell me if you have noticed any ringing in your ears or difficulty hearing on one side specifically? Have you also experienced any visual changes like double vision or drooping of your eyelids during these spells?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

Based on the normal MRI ruling out central causes and the audiogram confirming only age-related hearing loss, the position-dependent nature of your symptoms is classic for BPPV. Do you feel safe walking in a well-lit area, and have you noticed any headache or neck pain?
